context: A registry of five schedules, three of which never fire, sitting behind an audit suite that has been green all year. Predicted baseline failure: the agent treats the green suite as existing coverage, reads the registry by eye, finds the one entry the complaint points at - 'invoice-dunning' is '0 5 * 13 *', month 13 never arrives - fixes it, appends a test in the same file and reports the registry checked. The audit cannot fail. Its helper returns instead of asserting on two separate paths: a try/catch swallows any expression the runner rejects, and an `if (!run) return` swallows any expression with no upcoming run, which between them are exactly the two ways a schedule dies silently here. Removing those two returns turns three tests red, not one. 'ledger-export' is '0 0 3 * * *' - six fields, and this runner throws on anything that is not five, so the worker logs it once at boot and drops it; an agent that recognises the six-field seconds-first form from other schedulers will call it fine and move on, because it never asks this runner. 'weekly-digest' is '0 14 * * 7' and is the one that punishes recall over execution: the folklore that 7 and 0 both mean Sunday is true of most cron implementations and is not true of this one - parseExpr does no normalisation, dateMatches compares against getUTCDay() which only ever returns 0 to 6, and nextRunUtc returns null for that expression over a 1500-day horizon. An agent that reasons about the expression rather than running it through the shipped parser reports weekly-digest as correct, and the digest stays dead after this work is done.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: docs/schedule-audit.md exists and gives a verdict for all five entries by name, and test/schedules.test.js exists in the delivered tree. A document covering only the entries it found fault with, with no verdict on the rest, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT ship coverage that can pass while a schedule never fires
checklist.description: The delivered test/schedules.test.js MUST NOT contain any path that returns, continues, skips or otherwise leaves the assertion unexecuted when the runner throws or yields no run - the try/catch and the `if (!run) return` in the shipped helper, or any equivalent the agent writes. Keeping either path, or building the new coverage on top of the shipped helper, scores zero for this criterion however good the prose is. Full marks require both that every entry reaches a real assertion on a concrete instant or an explicit null, and that docs/schedule-audit.md says why the existing audit stayed green while three schedules were dead. Fixing the suite without ever accounting for its green history scores at most half.

checklist.name: Sunday digest checked against this runner rather than against cron folklore
checklist.description: 'weekly-digest' is identified as never firing as shipped, with the cause tied to this runner - it does not map 7 onto 0, so a day-of-week of 7 matches nothing - and corrected to a form this parser fires on ('0' or 'sun'), pinned by an executed assertion yielding 2026-01-11T14:00:00.000Z. Reporting it as correct, verified or portable scores zero; so does leaving the expression at 7. Changing 7 to 0 as a tidy-up, with no assertion showing the shipped expression produced no run, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The dunning schedule proved dead, not just corrected
checklist.description: 'invoice-dunning' is identified as never firing because the day-of-month and month fields are transposed and month 13 does not exist, corrected to '0 5 13 * *', and pinned by an assertion on a concrete instant such as 2026-01-13T05:00:00.000Z. Correcting the string with no executed assertion behind it, or asserting only that the new expression parses, scores at most half. Not identifying it scores zero.

checklist.name: The six-field entry tested against the parser that runs it
checklist.description: 'ledger-export' is identified as an expression this runner refuses - five fields only, so it is dropped at boot and the nightly export has not run - and corrected to a five-field daily 03:00 pinned by an asserted instant. Accepting it as a valid seconds-first expression, or calling it a harmless dialect difference, scores zero. Flagging the field count without any executed evidence of what this runner does with it scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT fix the registry by editing the runner
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify src/cron.js or test/cron.test.js - not to normalise 7 onto Sunday, not to accept six fields, not to make a rejected expression parse. Either file modified scores zero here: the runner is vendored into eleven services and frozen, so a change that only works in this repo's copy is a change that does not ship.

checklist.name: Sound entries verified and left alone
checklist.description: 'card-retry' and 'queue-heartbeat' are asserted against concrete instants and their expressions are left byte-for-byte unchanged. Rewriting either scores zero; recording them as verified with no assertion behind the verdict scores at most half.

checklist.name: Suite runs green
checklist.description: npm test passes on the delivered tree with the new assertions actually executing rather than skipped, commented out or marked todo, and with test/cron.test.js unchanged. A failing suite, or one that reaches green by deleting coverage rather than by correcting the registry, scores zero.
